mcqs.question: Consider the two reversible reactions at 298 K: (i) N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g)   ΔH = –92 kJ (exothermic) and (ii) CO(g) + H₂O(g) ⇌ CO₂(g) + H₂(g)   ΔH = +41 kJ (endothermic). If the temperature of each system is increased, which of the following correctly compares the shift in equilibrium for the two reactions?

options.A: Reaction (i) shifts to the left, while reaction (ii) shifts to the right.
options.B: Both reactions shift to the right.
options.C: Both reactions shift to the left.
options.D: Reaction (i) shifts to the right, while reaction (ii) shifts to the left.

mcqs.answer: Reaction (i) shifts to the left, while reaction (ii) shifts to the right.
mcqs.explanation: Increasing temperature adds heat to the system. For an exothermic reaction (ΔH < 0) the system treats heat as a product; adding heat shifts the equilibrium toward the reactants (left). For an endothermic reaction (ΔH > 0) heat is a reactant; adding heat shifts the equilibrium toward the products (right). Hence reaction (i) moves left and reaction (ii) moves right.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand effect of catalysts on equilibrium
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the effect of a catalyst on a chemical equilibrium system?

options.A: It lowers the equilibrium constant (K) of the reaction.
options.B: It speeds up the forward reaction more than the reverse reaction.
options.C: It speeds up both forward and reverse reactions equally, leaving the position of equilibrium unchanged.
options.D: It shifts the equilibrium toward the side with more moles of gas.

mcqs.answer: It speeds up both forward and reverse reactions equally, leaving the position of equilibrium unchanged.
mcqs.explanation: A catalyst provides an alternative pathway with lower activation energy for both forward and reverse reactions. Because both rates increase by the same factor, the ratio of forward to reverse rates (the equilibrium constant) remains unchanged, so the position of equilibrium does not shift.

mcqs.question: Le Chatelier’s principle states that when a system at equilibrium is subjected to a change in concentration, pressure, or temperature, the system will:

options.A: Shift in a direction that enhances the imposed change.
options.B: Shift in a direction that opposes the imposed change.
options.C: Remain unchanged because equilibrium is a fixed state.
options.D: Always shift toward the side with more moles of gas.

mcqs.answer: Shift in a direction that opposes the imposed change.
mcqs.explanation: Le Chatelier’s principle predicts that an equilibrium system counteracts any external disturbance. By shifting in the opposite direction, the system reduces the effect of the change and re‑establishes a new equilibrium.

mcqs.question: In the equilibrium N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), what will be the effect of adding more H₂(g) to the system at constant temperature and pressure?

options.A: The equilibrium will shift to the left, decreasing NH₃ concentration.
options.B: The equilibrium will shift to the right, increasing NH₃ concentration.
options.C: There will be no shift; only the total pressure changes.
options.D: The reaction quotient Q will become larger than K, causing the reaction to stop.

mcqs.answer: The equilibrium will shift to the right, increasing NH₃ concentration.
mcqs.explanation: Adding H₂ increases the concentration of a reactant. According to Le Chatelier’s principle, the system responds by consuming the added reactant, i.e., shifting toward the products (right) to re‑establish equilibrium, thereby increasing NH₃ concentration.

mcqs.question: For the gaseous equilibrium 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), how does an increase in total pressure (at constant temperature) affect the position of equilibrium?

options.A: The equilibrium shifts to the side with more moles of gas.
options.B: The equilibrium shifts to the side with fewer moles of gas.
options.C: Pressure changes have no effect on the equilibrium position.
options.D: The equilibrium constant Kp increases with pressure.

mcqs.answer: The equilibrium shifts to the side with fewer moles of gas.
mcqs.explanation: On the left side there are 3 moles of gas (2 SO₂ + 1 O₂) and on the right side 2 moles (2 SO₃). Raising pressure favors the side with fewer gas molecules, so the equilibrium shifts right, reducing total moles.

mcqs.question: A student observes that the yield of NH₃ in the Haber process decreases when the reactor temperature is raised from 400 °C to 500 °C. Which of the following best explains this observation?

options.A: The equilibrium constant Kc increases with temperature for this exothermic reaction.
options.B: Higher temperature increases the rate of the forward reaction more than the reverse reaction.
options.C: The reaction is exothermic; raising temperature shifts the equilibrium toward the reactants, reducing NH₃ yield.
options.D: Increasing temperature adds more reactant molecules, thus decreasing product formation.

mcqs.answer: The reaction is exothermic; raising temperature shifts the equilibrium toward the reactants, reducing NH₃ yield.
mcqs.explanation: The Haber process (N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃) is exothermic (ΔH < 0). According to Le Chatelier’s principle, adding heat (raising temperature) shifts the equilibrium toward the endothermic direction, i.e., the reactants, thereby lowering the amount of NH₃ formed.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand effect of catalysts on equilibrium
mcqs.question: In the industrial synthesis of sulfuric acid, the contact process uses V₂O₅ as a catalyst for the reaction 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g). Which statement correctly reflects the role of V₂O₅ in this equilibrium?

options.A: V₂O₅ increases the equilibrium constant, producing more SO₃ at equilibrium.
options.B: V₂O₅ lowers the activation energy for both forward and reverse reactions, allowing the system to reach equilibrium faster without changing the equilibrium composition.
options.C: V₂O₅ shifts the equilibrium toward the products by adsorbing SO₂ molecules.
options.D: V₂O₅ acts as a reactant that is consumed during the formation of SO₃.

mcqs.answer: V₂O₅ lowers the activation energy for both forward and reverse reactions, allowing the system to reach equilibrium faster without changing the equilibrium composition.
mcqs.explanation: The catalyst V₂O₅ provides an alternative pathway with lower activation energy for both directions of the reaction. It speeds up the rate at which equilibrium is attained but does not alter the value of the equilibrium constant or the final composition of the mixture.

mcqs.question: A sealed container holds the equilibrium mixture for the reaction N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) at 300 K. The container is then heated to 350 K while the volume remains unchanged. According to Le Chatelier’s principle, which of the following best describes the system’s response?

options.A: The equilibrium shifts to the right, producing more NH₃ because temperature increase favors product formation.
options.B: The equilibrium shifts to the left, producing more N₂ and H₂ because the forward reaction is exothermic.
options.C: The equilibrium position does not change because pressure is constant.
options.D: The catalyst present in the container will prevent any shift in equilibrium.

mcqs.answer: The equilibrium shifts to the left, producing more N₂ and H₂ because the forward reaction is exothermic.
mcqs.explanation: The forward reaction (formation of NH₃) releases heat (exothermic). Raising temperature adds heat, so the system counteracts by shifting the equilibrium toward the reactants (left) to absorb the added heat, decreasing NH₃ concentration. Volume (pressure) and catalyst do not affect the direction of the shift.
